prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” lawyer for every car wreck — the right attorney depends on the details of your crash, injuries, insurance issues, and whether you want a trial attorney or someone who primarily settles claims. I can help you find a good match. Below are practical steps, criteria to use, and questions to ask so you can pick the best lawyer for your case.

Quick actions
- Act quickly: in Texas the statute of limitations for most injury claims is 2 years from the accident date (there are exceptions).  
- If you want, tell me your Houston zip code and a few details (seriousness of injuries, at-fault party insured/uninsured, whether police report exists) and I’ll compile a short list of well-reviewed local attorneys to contact.

How to evaluate a “best” car-wreck (personal injury) lawyer
Look for:
- Substantial experience with car-accident cases and plaintiff-side experience.
- Trial experience or a record of large settlements/verdicts if your case may need litigation.
- Board certification in personal injury trial law (if available) — a sign of recognized expertise.
- Good client communication and a local courtroom presence (familiarity with Houston judges/juries).
- Adequate resources (investigators, medical experts) to build your case.
- Contingency-fee agreement (common: attorney is paid only if you recover).

Where to check credentials and reviews
- State Bar of Texas lawyer search (disciplinary history, license status).
- Peer-review sites: Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers.
- Client review sites and Google/BBB reviews (read patterns, not isolated comments).
- Ask for references from former clients or case results.

Key questions to ask during a free consultation
1. How long have you handled car-accident/personal-injury cases?  
2. What percentage of your practice is plaintiff personal injury?  
3. Have you tried similar cases to verdict? Can you give examples of settlements/verdicts?  
4. Who will handle my case day-to-day (partner/associate/paralegal)?  
5. What is your fee structure and typical percentage? Are there any upfront costs I’ll be responsible for?  
6. How do you communicate (phone, email)? What’s the expected response time?  
7. Do you work on contingency? How are costs and expenses handled if we don’t win?  
8. What is your strategy for my case and likely timeline?  
9. Do you have the resources to investigate and litigate if needed?  
10. Can you provide client references?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or outcome.  
- Pushy or high-pressure tactics to sign immediately.  
- No written fee agreement or unwillingness to put terms in writing.  
- Poor responsiveness during your initial contacts.  
- No trial experience if your case might require litigation.

Typical fee expectations in Texas
- Many PI lawyers handle car wrecks on contingency (commonly around one-third of recovery if settled before suit, sometimes higher if a suit is filed or appealed). Always get the exact percentage in writing and ask about additional expenses.

If you want specific names
Tell me your Houston zip code, the nature/severity of your injuries, and whether the at-fault driver had insurance. I’ll put together a short list of well-reviewed Houston personal injury lawyers who handle car wrecks and match your needs.
